back: Average the returns observed after visits to $s$: $V(s)\leftarrow V(s)+\alpha(G_t-V(s))$.
First-visit uses only the first visit to $s$ per episode; every-visit uses all visits. Both converge to $V^\pi$.
Needs terminating episodes, updates only at the end, high variance, and states that are never visited are never learned.
$r_{t+1}+\gamma V(s_{t+1})-V(s_t)$: zero in expectation at the true value function.
Updating an estimate using another estimate (the next state's value) rather than a complete observed return.
MC target: unbiased, high variance. TD target: lower variance, biased by the current estimate (bias shrinks as learning proceeds).
$Q(s,a)\leftarrow Q+\alpha[r+\gamma Q(s',a')-Q(s,a)]$ with $a'$ the action actually taken; on-policy.
On-policy: learn the value of the policy that generates the data. Off-policy: learn about a target policy (e.g. greedy) from data of a different behaviour policy.
Q-learning learns the shortest path along the cliff edge but falls during exploration; SARSA learns a safer longer path and earns more online reward.

front: What to do at a terminal transition
back: Drop the bootstrap term: target $=r$ (the value of a terminal state is 0).
$\sum\alpha_t=\infty$ and $\sum\alpha_t^2<\infty$ guarantee convergence of tabular TD; constant small $\alpha$ is used in practice.
